ideal: Raise scores across the board and keep best=A — this was an exceptionally active evidence day with two 10pt single-stock gaps vs a flat index plus three substantive filings, so nearly every candidate answer already does solid work on the only choices that really mattered.

verdicts.note: All five events delivered: both big moves with index beside them, Apple's earnings 8-K and both 10-Ks, all in plain words. The two judged calls — guessing Meta filed at 08:00 before the close for a +10.4% print, and treating Apple 'quarterly or annual results' as earnings — are the right reads of ambiguous evidence.
verdicts.answer:
Microsoft fell 9.99% on a day the S&P 500 fell 0.2% — no filing explains it yet.
Meta rose 10.4% on a day the S&P 500 fell 0.2% — no filing explains it yet.
Apple filed its quarterly results (8-K): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019326000005/aapl-20260129.htm
Meta and Tesla filed their annual 10-K reports: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm · https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026003952/tsla-20251231.htm

verdicts.note: Faultless on the price moves, with index context and an honest 'no filing explains it yet' (the Meta 10-K is an annual report, not a same-day price driver and A already explains why). But it drops Apple's earnings 8-K and the two 10-Ks — exactly the material filings she says she wants — so completeness sustains the main penalty.
verdicts.answer:
Microsoft fell 9.99% vs S&P 500 fell 0.2%, no filing explains it yet
Meta rose 10.4% vs S&P 500 fell 0.2%, no filing explains it yet

verdicts.note: Covers everything and every number matches. Two genuine faults: the Meta line juxtaposes the 10-K with the +10.4% move in a way that asks to be read as cause when a 10-K alone does not explain a jump, and it never says anything about earnings for Apple while formatting the index as '-0.2%' with a raw minus sign instead of the words she asked for.
verdicts.answer:
Microsoft fell 9.99% vs S&P 500 -0.2%; no filing explains it yet  
Meta Platforms rose 10.4% vs S&P 500 -0.2%; 10‑K filing (annual report) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm  
Apple 8‑K filing (earnings) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019326000005/aapl-20260129.htm  
Tesla 10‑K filing (annual report) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026003952/tsla-20251231.htm

verdicts.note: The 'nearly 10 percentage points' read survives scrutiny as a fair rounding of vs_index_pts -9.79 rather than an invented number, and calling out Apple's 8-K as having no price move is useful. But it loses Meta's filing link, drops Tesla's 10-K entirely, and leans into editorial flourish ('massive') over her preferred bare numbers.
verdicts.answer:
**Microsoft** dropped 9.99%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.2% — a massive underperformance of nearly 10 percentage points. No filing explains it yet.

**Meta** surged 10.4%, vs. the S&P 500 down 0.2%. A 10-K (annual report) was filed the same day.

**Apple** filed an 8-K reporting quarterly/annual earnings results. No price move in the report.
